intuition.title: Powder and film use different charges
intuition.text: The powder recipe uses 0.10 g TiF4 and 160 °C for 24 h. The coloured film uses 0.010 g TiF4, adds 5 mL tert-butyl alcohol and reacts at 130 °C for 24 h with titanium foil present. Vessel capacity is 50 mL in both protocols, not a reported liquid volume.

intuition.title: Early precursor, sheets and stacks are different objects
intuition.text: The 3 h material is an amorphous organic-rich titanium precursor. Later crystallinity, lamellar spacing, plate thickness and overall assembly dimensions describe different structural levels. The source supplies fixed temperature and stoichiometry for the time series, but does not separately restate each absolute charge.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 time series; SI PDF p. 3, Figure S3

intuition.title: Stoichiometry changes assembly
intuition.text: Ratios TiF4:benzyl alcohol = 1:4800, 1:1200, 1:600 and 1:240 are separate comparisons at 160 °C for 24 h. A useful range 1:2400 to 1:300 is stated in the discussion, not a list of individually measured specimens. High fluoride loading is proposed to generate excess HF that etches (001) facets; neither HF concentration nor this mechanism is directly measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Ratio discussion; SI PDF p. 2, Figure S2

intuition.title: Surface-mediated assembly is an author model
intuition.text: Figure 3 proposes benzyl groups and π stacking between sheets. The text gives adjacent surface Ti separation about 0.4 nm and model interlayer spacing 0.92 nm; the diagram also labels 0.38 and 0.76 nm along the surface. These are model dimensions, distinct from the approximately 1.3 nm HRTEM spacing in the 5 h specimen. No source coordinates or unit-cell model are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 3 and model discussion

intuition.title: Alcohol identity affects stacking
intuition.text: Pentafluorobenzyl alcohol alone gives no sheets or stacking. Its 1:1 v/v mixture with benzyl alcohol restores organized stacks with a reported gap of 5 ± 2 nm. Among the para-halogen examples, fluoro gives stacked sheets while chloro and bromo give sheets without stacking. Substituent size and aromatic interactions are the authors’ explanations, not measured molecular structures. Aliphatic-alcohol negative observations retain their missing separate conditions.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Alcohol discussion; SI PDF p. 4–5, Figures S5–S6

intuition.title: Organic content and FTIR comparisons
intuition.text: Figure S3 reports losses of 78, 64, 43, 38, 33 and 24% at reaction times 3, 5, 8, 12, 18 and 24 h, respectively. Its printed axis convention is retained. The authors assign 1489 cm−1 to aromatic rings and broad features at 3010 and 2893 cm−1 to interactions at the TiO2 surface. The latter features are absent for physisorbed benzyl alcohol on commercial P25. Figure S4 includes 12 h and 24 h products, pure P25, adsorbed P25 and pure benzyl alcohol. Adsorption preparation is unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, TGA and FTIR discussion; SI PDF p. 3–4, Figures S3–S4

intuition.title: Colour and substrate scope
intuition.text: The green layered film on Ti foil is 190 ± 10 nm thick and has diffuse-reflectance bands near 400 and 640 nm. Conditions for every observed colour are not supplied. The sol-gel procedure explicitly coats glass, whereas its heading, main comparison and Figure S8 refer to Ti foil. The relationship is unresolved; comparison thickness is not silently assigned to the glass specimen.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4 and sol-gel comparison; SI PDF p. 1, 6, Sol-gel preparation and Figure S8

intuition.title: Background and incomplete alternatives
intuition.text: Introductory photovoltaic, photocatalytic and reflective-coating applications are motivation or prospective uses, not performance measurements of these samples. Reference note 15 says titanium alkoxides behave similarly when HF is added, but gives no complete additional recipe. Cited full sources are unreviewed.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Introduction, conclusion and reference note 15

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
